messages:
Sara K: FYI: ACME reported spikes of 429s starting after last night's rate-limit push. They're seeing both 429s and higher latency on generation endpoints.
Devon: Can you paste a sample request id and timestamps? We pushed the staged limit change at 03:10 UTC (10% rollout to us-west2).
Sara K: req_id=01H8ZB9X-abc123, customer timestamp 2025-09-15T03:22:11Z. They say it affects batch jobs that burst ~300 reqs/min.
Lex: Are they on hosted tier or dedicated? If hosted, the default pipeline limit was reduced from 120->60 qps per-token bucket in that rollout.
Sara K: Hosted (team-acme-prod). They were at ~100 qps pre-change.
AJ: oncall-bot shows a rise in 429 rate for us-west2 around rollout window :eyes:
oncall-bot: ALERT: rate_limiter_429_rate increased by 6.2x in prod/us-west2 between 03:10-03:30 UTC.
Devon: Sara, can you ask them to run a curl that includes the request id header and dump response headers? Example:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-Id: 01H8ZB9X-abc123" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"test","max_tokens":20}'
```
We want X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset values.
Sara K: Sent that to customer, they returned this header snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1694779330
Retry-After: 15
```
Lex: Confirms the new limit is applied. Looks like token-bucket burst wasn't large enough for their job.
Devon: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Roll back staged policy for hosted tier in us-west2, 2) Add temporary burst allowance for the customer (whitelist), 3) Ask customer to add exponential backoff + jitter.
Support Lead: We should coordinate rollback only if rollback won't cause global regressions. Can SRE confirm capacity headroom?
AJ: SRE pinged infra team, capacity dashboard shows headroom ~18% in us-west2 but that assumes even distribution. If a few customers burst, we risk hotspots.
Lex: Proposal: rollback the rollout at 0:00 UTC (now) for the staged policy in us-west2, then re-run with a higher burst ceiling (allow short bursts up to 120 qps) and instrument per-tenant throttles.
Sara K: Customer asked for immediate fix. They can wait 15-30m if we can whitelist them now.
Devon: Quick whitelist route: infra-cli policies whitelist add --tenant team-acme-prod --region us-west2 --burst=120
AJ: I'll run that and monitor. Tagging @oncall-bot to create a temporary incident and add observability checks.
oncall-bot: Incident #INC-20250915-21 created: Temporary whitelist + policy rollback monitoring. Notifying eng-platform + eng-sre.
Devon: Ran whitelist command at 03:36 UTC. I also put a canary rollback in the pipeline in case we need full rollback: infra-cli rollout rollback --policy rate_limit_tier_default --region us-west2 --staged
Lex: After whitelist, customer reports errors dropped to 1-2/min and latency back to baseline. :thumbsup:
Support Lead: Great. Next steps:
- Devon: keep whitelist for 2h, monitor token-meter and 429 rate (SLO 0.1% 429)
- Lex: prepare a patch to adjust burst config and add per-tenant leak bucket
- Sara K: follow-up with ACME about recommended client-side backoff
- AJ: confirm rollback timeline and coordinate if we need global rollback
Devon: Logging note for postmortem: rollout diffing didn't include per-tenant burst profile, need to add that to rollout checklist.
Sara K: I'll update the customer thread and close once SLOs stable.
AJ: Leave this thread open for 2h. If anything changes ping #eng-oncall.
Support Lead: Thanks team, good ops. :heart:
